title: Where Did the Rate Change? — Page CUSUM, A. F. M. Smith (1975) Posterior Changepoint Probabilities & Carlin–Gelfand–Smith Gibbs Sampling Across 112 Years of British Coal-Mining Disasters

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: Between 1851 and 1962, fatal British coal-mining disasters suddenly dropped from ~3 per year to ~0.9 per year—when did safety rules actually bend the curve? Bayesian changepoint models compute a full probability curve across candidate years instead of guessing a single date.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Whenever hospitals, factories, or climate sensors look for when a rate shifted, reporting a posterior window over the changepoint prevents false certainty around noisy counts.
keyTakeaways: Modeling yearly disaster counts as Poisson(lambda_1) up to year k and Poisson(lambda_2) after year k turns historical regime detection into an explicit likelihood across k = 1..n.
A. F. M. Smith (1975) and Carlin, Gelfand & Smith (1992) used conjugate Gamma priors and Gibbs sampling to compute exact marginal posteriors for k, lambda_1, and lambda_2.

On Maguire/Jarrett's 112-year British coal-mining ledger, posterior probability concentrates around ~1889–1892—lining up with the Coal Mines Regulation Act era—while honestly showing multi-year uncertainty.

vocab.meaning: The unknown time index where a data-generating process switches from an initial parameter regime to a new one.
Pairing Poisson event counts with Gamma rate priors so posterior rate distributions stay closed-form Gamma.
An MCMC algorithm that cycles through sampling each unknown parameter conditionally on the latest values of the others.

quiz.question: Why is a posterior probability distribution over changepoint year k more informative than picking the single year with the lowest p-value?
options: It quantifies exact uncertainty across neighboring candidate years and averages rate estimates over plausible switch dates
It forces lambda_1 and lambda_2 to be equal
quiz.explanation: Adjacent years often share substantial posterior mass because annual Poisson counts are noisy; integrating over k propagates date uncertainty honestly.
